title: Thin JetBrains adapter
description: Objective: let JetBrains discover/start the daemon and open/embed or browser-fallback to the standalone control room. Deliverable: a thin adapter with no duplicated product logic. NOT in scope: canonical state, lifecycle transitions, separate board implementation, or VS Code parity. Hard dependencies: standalone Control-room journey gate and Distribution manifest packaging. Owned paths: adapters/jetbrains/**. Verification: adapter-specific tests plus pnpm test:integration.
definitionOfDone: Adapter discovers compatible daemon/control-room distributions and fails closed on mismatch.
All product actions and rendering come from the standalone app/generated contracts.
Start, open, embed, browser fallback, reconnect, and uninstall cases pass.
taskRails: Portability consumes frozen daemon/core contracts; adapters cannot fork lifecycle or authority semantics.
Official MCP stdio and Streamable HTTP only; no custom MCP-over-WebSocket dialect.
Unsupported OS/provider/import facts remain typed UNSUPPORTED or UNKNOWN, never guessed.
IDE adapters are thin optional shells for the standalone control room. Keep files below 400 lines and use explicit owned paths.

THE CONTRACT, adapters/ide-contract/src/index.ts (234 lines, committed at HEAD, package name `@moe/ide-adapter-contract`):
  values  IDE_ADAPTER_LAYER, IDE_ADAPTER_LAYERS (IDE_ADAPTER, DAEMON_DISCOVERY_PORT, DAEMON_START_PORT, CONTROL_ROOM_OPEN_PORT), IDE_ADAPTER_REASON_CODES (14 codes: DAEMON_RUNNING, DAEMON_ABSENT, DAEMON_STATE_UNKNOWN, DAEMON_DISCOVERY_REFUSED, DAEMON_ENDPOINT_MISSING, DAEMON_STARTED, DAEMON_START_UNVERIFIED, DAEMON_START_REFUSED, CONTROL_ROOM_EMBEDDED, CONTROL_ROOM_BROWSER_FALLBACK, CONTROL_ROOM_ASSETS_MISSING, CONTROL_ROOM_BROWSER_REFUSED, CONTROL_ROOM_OPEN_UNKNOWN, EVIDENCE_MALFORMED)
  decisions  decideDaemonDiscovery(evidence), decideDaemonStart(evidence), decideControlRoomOpen(evidence)
  ports  DaemonDiscoveryPort.probeDaemon(), DaemonStartPort.startDaemon(), ControlRoomOpenPort.openControlRoom(), bundled as IdeAdapterPorts
  results IdeAdapterResult = IdeAdapterSuccess | IdeAdapterFailure
Do NOT add a reason code, a layer, or a fourth decision function. If a JetBrains fault does not map to an existing code, that is a finding to report, not a licence to widen the frozen vocabulary.

Compose that refusal vocabulary for mismatch; do not invent a compatibility verdict.

Confirm the gap: `ls adapters/jetbrains` -> No such file or directory. Confirm the harness already collects adapters tests: vitest.config.ts include contains "adapters/**/*.test.ts". Record the baseline gate.

implementationPlan.description:
Create the workspace package: adapters/jetbrains/package.json and tsconfig.json, as a SIBLING of adapters/ide-contract under the existing `adapters/*` glob (pnpm-workspace.yaml already resolves it; do NOT edit that file, its comment already names this task as the owner of adapters/jetbrains/**).

package.json mirrors the contract package's shape: name `@moe/jetbrains-adapter`, private, type module, exports { ".": "./src/index.ts" }, scripts typecheck (`tsc --project tsconfig.json`) and test (`vitest run --root ../.. adapters/jetbrains/src`). Dependencies: `@moe/ide-adapter-contract`: "workspace:*" and `@moe/contracts`: "workspace:*".

THE DEPENDENCY EDGE IS THE DELIVERABLE HERE, not a formality — this task is the Clause 1 consumer edge that task-c2d92880 named. Prove it three ways after `pnpm install`, exactly as the board rail requires: the manifest declaration, the pnpm-lock.yaml importer entry for adapters/jetbrains, and a compiled bare-specifier probe from the package root resolving `@moe/ide-adapter-contract`. Three tasks died on this board today for skipping the edge and assuming the symbol.

tsconfig extends ../../tsconfig.base.json with rootDir ".", a tsbuildinfo path under node_modules/.cache, types ["node"], include ["src/**/*.ts"]. pnpm-lock.yaml will change; it is shared state — verify its diff contains ONLY the new importer before committing.

TDD RED. Create adapters/jetbrains/src/jetbrains-adapter.test.ts driving the not-yet-written adapter with INJECTED fake ports — no real daemon spawn, no real browser launch, no network. DoD 3 names six cases and each must be separately asserted with the EXACT reason code AND the refusing layer from the contract's frozen tuples:
  - START: daemon absent -> start -> DAEMON_STARTED.
  - OPEN/EMBED: assets present and embedding available -> CONTROL_ROOM_EMBEDDED.
  - BROWSER FALLBACK: embedding unavailable -> CONTROL_ROOM_BROWSER_FALLBACK, NOT a failure. This is the case most likely to be modelled wrongly as an error.
  - RECONNECT: a daemon already running is discovered without starting a second one -> DAEMON_RUNNING, and assert startDaemon was NOT called. "It reconnected" is only proven by the port not firing.
  - UNINSTALL: after teardown the adapter holds no live handle and a subsequent action refuses rather than silently reopening.
  - MISMATCH (DoD 1): an incompatible distribution manifest fails CLOSED using the @moe/contracts distribution refusal vocabulary, never an optimistic proceed.
Also: a port that THROWS becomes a typed failure at that port's layer, never an escaping exception; and DAEMON_START_UNVERIFIED (started but listening unconfirmed) is a refusal, not a success. Assert the sweep over IDE_ADAPTER_REASON_CODES produced a NON-ZERO case count.

GREEN: adapters/jetbrains/src/index.ts plus its one-line LF `.js` bridge (`export * from "./index.ts";`, matching adapters/ide-contract/src/index.js byte-for-byte in form). This is the thin session that sequences the contract's three decisions and adds ONLY what the contract deliberately left out: distribution compatibility, reconnect, and uninstall.

Sequence: check distribution compatibility FIRST and refuse closed on mismatch (DoD 1) — an incompatible pair must never reach discovery; then probeDaemon -> decideDaemonDiscovery; if DAEMON_ABSENT, startDaemon -> decideDaemonStart; then openControlRoom -> decideControlRoomOpen. Return the contract's IdeAdapterResult unchanged; do not re-wrap or re-code its verdicts.

RECONNECT is defined by absence of action: when discovery reports a running daemon, the start port must NOT be invoked. UNINSTALL/teardown drops the session's handles so a later action refuses instead of silently reopening.

THIN MEANS THIN (taskRail 1 and 4, and DoD 2): no canonical state, no lifecycle transitions, no board implementation, no product rendering. All product actions and rendering come from the standalone control room and the generated client — do NOT reimplement packages/control-room-client and do not fork lifecycle or authority semantics. Wrap every port call so a throw becomes a typed failure at that port's layer.

Keep below 400 lines (this epic's rail); if the compatibility gate and the session together approach it, split the gate into its own module rather than growing the file.

Prove the composition edge is real, not nominal (Clause 1, and the reason this task was promoted). Add a runtime-entrypoint test at adapters/jetbrains/src/jetbrains-runtime-entrypoint.test.ts copying the proven mechanism from adapters/ide-contract/src/ide-adapter-runtime-entrypoint.test.ts: `execFileAsync(process.execPath, ["--experimental-strip-types", "--input-type=module", "-e", source], { cwd: PACKAGE_ROOT, timeout })`, cwd at the package root so the bare specifier resolves through this package's own exports map via Node's self-reference rule.

Assert BOTH: that `@moe/jetbrains-adapter` imports with named exports and undefinedBindingCount 0, AND that `@moe/ide-adapter-contract` resolves FROM this package — the second is what proves the dependency edge rather than a copied symbol. Include the negative control from the reference: an unbridged test module fails with the literal ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND, proving the probe can still detect failure. Remember `--experimental-strip-types` ERASES `export type`, so only the contract's VALUE exports (the code tuple, the layer tuple, the three decide* functions) are observable at runtime — assert on those.

Mutation drills, then restore byte-exact. Each must redden a NAMED test; record the failing assertion text. (a) Skip the distribution compatibility gate so an incompatible pair proceeds — the DoD 1 mismatch case must redden; this is the fail-closed property the epic rail names. (b) Call startDaemon even when discovery reports DAEMON_RUNNING — the reconnect case must redden, proving it asserts the port was NOT called rather than merely that the result looked right. (c) Map CONTROL_ROOM_BROWSER_FALLBACK to a failure — the fallback case must redden, proving fallback is modelled as a success path. (d) Treat DAEMON_START_UNVERIFIED as success — that case must redden. (e) Change only the refusing LAYER on one port failure, leaving the code — a layer assertion must redden independently. (f) Let a port throw escape unwrapped — the typed-failure case must redden.

Every file here is NEW and untracked, so `git diff` is structurally blind to them; hash with `git hash-object` before and after rather than trusting an empty diff, and re-run the suite after each restore because a foreign whole-tree completion hook can commit a drill edit while `git status` looks clean.

Verify and self-review. (1) Run the adapter gate: `pnpm --filter @moe/jetbrains-adapter typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/jetbrains-adapter test`, then the task's stated verification `pnpm test:integration`. Confirm the root `pnpm test` collects your files — vitest.config.ts already includes "adapters/**/*.test.ts", so the Test Files count must GROW; if it does not, your tests are not being collected and every DoD item is certified by a suite that never ran. (2) Hand-measure each new file with `grep -c ''` against this epic's 400-line rail. (3) Path-attributed baseline: repo-wide typecheck and test at merge-base and HEAD, intersect the failing-path delta with owned paths, confirm EMPTY, disclose foreign red verbatim. (4) Adversarial review: is any product logic, canonical state, lifecycle transition or rendering duplicated here rather than delegated (DoD 2, taskRail 1)? Did I add a reason code, layer, or decision function to the frozen contract vocabulary? Is browser fallback a success rather than an error? Does reconnect prove the start port was never called? Does any path proceed on an incompatible or unverifiable distribution? Is there any MCP dialect other than official stdio / Streamable HTTP (taskRail 2)? Does any unsupported OS or provider fact get guessed instead of staying typed UNSUPPORTED/UNKNOWN (taskRail 3)? (5) Confirm the `.js` bridge exists with a trailing LF via `od -c`. (6) Stage by explicit pathspec over the six owned paths plus pnpm-lock.yaml, then `git diff --cached --name-only` to confirm nothing foreign is staged — the index on this board is shared. Record in completion notes that this closes the Clause 1 consumer edge for task-c2d92880989b4ed2bc76494ee6979d91.
